Part III — The Reasoning Model
Module
9
·
The
Thinking
Cycle™
The Thinking Cycle™ is the cognitive engine of Jurassic English™. It is a four-phase progression — Analyze,
Evaluate, Justify, Reﬂect — through which every literary text at every level is processed. It is not a lesson plan; it
is the underlying cognitive architecture that the Four-Lesson Cycle (Part IV) instantiates as a teaching sequence.
The trainer must understand and convey that the Thinking Cycle™ is not optional, not adaptable in sequence,
and not subject to teacher preference. A lesson that begins with Justify before completing Analyze and Evaluate
is not a Jurassic English™ lesson. The phases must run in order, and each must be visibly completed before the
next begins.

Rubric is the framework's instrument for measuring cognitive progression. It maps directly to Bloom's
Taxonomy and is used by trainers, educators, and the DRE to grade student work consistently across all ﬁve
levels.

Reasoning Levels are not equivalent to grade levels. A Level 1 (Foundation) student is regularly pushed to
Reasoning Level 2 and 3 within the boundaries of oral discourse. A Level 5 (Advanced) student is expected to
operate consistently at Reasoning Levels 5 and 6. The trainer must teach educators to set Reasoning Level
targets per lesson, not per student tier — every lesson plan in the framework explicitly names its target
Reasoning Level.
Module
11
·
Regulation-Before-Reasoning
Regulation-Before-Reasoning is the structural precondition for higher-order cognition in the Jurassic English™
classroom. Every lesson at every level begins with a physiological regulation activity. This is not warm-up time.
It is not optional. It is the architectural foundation of the cognitive work that follows.
Blueprint v3.5 systematically integrates explicit instruction in interoception — the internal physiological sense
that allows learners to notice bodily sensations and translate them into emotional meaning. Research
demonstrates that 8–10 weeks of targeted interoceptive practice signiﬁcantly elevates students' capacity to
self-regulate, reducing oﬀ-task behaviour and increasing engagement with complex tasks. For neurodivergent
learners — students with ASD, ADHD, or trauma backgrounds — the regulation phase is the single intervention
that makes the rest of the framework accessible.

Module
12
·
Accountable
Talk
Accountable Talk is the discourse architecture of the Jurassic English™ classroom. It comprises three core
moves that begin as teacher language at Foundation and Development levels and progressively become
student language by Expansion (Level 3) and beyond. By Level 5, students are expected to deploy these moves
independently, without prompting, in every Socratic seminar.

can you say more?"

Pressing "But have you considered…?" Forces a student to deepen reasoning
and confront alternatives

The trainer audits Accountable Talk by counting moves. In a calibrated Level 3 lesson, no fewer than three
Pressing moves should be heard during the Strata phase. In a calibrated Level 5 seminar, at least 70% of the
moves should originate from students rather than from the educator. These are diagnostic numbers — when
they fall, the lesson has decayed below ﬁdelity, and the trainer must intervene.
